title: MDAgents: An Adaptive Collaboration of LLMs for Medical Decision-Making
abstract-summary: Adaptive multi-agent framework that assigns solo or group collaboration structures to LLM teams based on medical task complexity; best in 7/10 benchmarks.
notes: Up to 4.2% improvement over best prior; 11.8% avg gain from moderator+knowledge in group collaboration

title: MedAgents: Large Language Models as Collaborators for Zero-shot Medical Reasoning
abstract-summary: Role-playing LLM agents participate in multi-round discussion for zero-shot medical reasoning across 9 datasets.
notes: 6.1pp average improvement across MedQA/MedMCQA/PubMedQA/MMLU subtasks

title: ArgMed-Agents: Explainable Clinical Decision Reasoning with LLM Discussion via Argumentation Schemes
abstract-summary: Multi-agent argumentation framework for explainable clinical decision reasoning; uses symbolic solver to identify rational arguments.
notes: Improves accuracy and explainability over CoT; specific numbers require full paper access

title: Catfish Agent: Disrupting Agreement Bias in Multi-Agent LLMs for Clinical Decision Making
abstract-summary: Introduces a dissent-injecting agent to counter silent agreement in multi-agent medical QA; 12.73pp avg improvement.
notes: 39.2% relative gain over DeepSeek-R1; outperforms GPT-4o and prior multi-agent frameworks on 9 QA and 3 VQA benchmarks

title: MediHive: A Decentralized Agent Collective for Medical Reasoning
abstract-summary: Decentralized multi-agent framework with shared memory pool and iterative fusion; agents self-assign roles and conduct evidence-based debates.
notes: 7.3pp over strongest single-agent; also 78.4% on PubMedQA

title: MedARC: Adaptive Multi-Agent Refinement and Collaboration for Enhanced Medical Reasoning
abstract-summary: Multi-agent debate with structured inter-agent summarization and confidence-aware aggregation for medical QA.
notes: 4.3pp improvement; mitigates hallucinations and fragmented reasoning

title: Collaborative Intelligence in AI: Evaluating the Performance of a Council of AIs on the USMLE
abstract-summary: Five GPT-4 agents with a facilitator iteratively discuss and reach consensus on 325 USMLE questions.
notes: 97%/93%/94% on Steps 1/2CK/3; 83% consensus accuracy on initially contested questions

title: AgentClinic: A Multimodal Agent Benchmark to Evaluate AI in Simulated Clinical Environments
abstract-summary: Multi-agent clinical simulation benchmark with patient/doctor/examiner agents; accuracy drops to 1/10 of static QA format.
notes: Diagnostic accuracy much lower in interactive vs static format; bias reduces accuracy further

title: Enhancing Diagnostic Capability with Multi-Agents Conversational Large Language Models
abstract-summary: MAC framework inspired by clinical MDT discussions for rare disease diagnosis on 302 cases.
notes: MAC with 4 doctors + supervisor outperforms CoT/Self-Refine/Self-Consistency; optimal at 4 agents

title: Orchestrated Multi Agents Sustain Accuracy Under Clinical-Scale Workloads Compared to a Single Agent
abstract-summary: Orchestrated multi-agent system vs single agent under clinical workloads of 5-80 concurrent tasks.
notes: Single-agent collapses to 16.6% at 80 tasks while multi-agent holds at 65.3%; 65x token reduction

title: Deliberative Multi-Agent Large Language Models Improve Clinical Reasoning in Ophthalmology
abstract-summary: Multi-agent councils of 4 LLMs with peer review on 100 ophthalmology vignettes; 3 tiers tested.
notes: Proprietary flagship: 95.0 vs 90.8; open-source: 91.0 vs 83.2; consistent improvement across tiers

title: MedLA: A Logic-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Complex Medical Reasoning with Large Language Models
abstract-summary: Logic-driven multi-agent with syllogistic trees and cross-agent discussion for medical reasoning.
notes: 11.1pp gain (8B); 10.1pp gain (70B: 51.9 vs 41.8); no fine-tuning or retrieval needed

title: MAM: Modular Multi-Agent Framework for Multi-Modal Medical Diagnosis via Role-Specialized Collaboration
abstract-summary: Modular framework with GP/Specialist/Radiologist/Assistant/Director agents for multimodal medical diagnosis.
notes: 18-365% improvement over baseline models; optimal at 3 specialized roles

title: Expertise-aware Multi-LLM Recruitment and Collaboration for Medical Decision-Making
abstract-summary: Two-stage framework: expertise-aware recruitment then confidence/adversarial-driven collaboration.
notes: 2.69pp over best closed-source model; evaluated on 3 public MDM datasets

title: Do Mixed-Vendor Multi-Agent LLMs Improve Clinical Diagnosis?
abstract-summary: Compares single-LLM / single-vendor / mixed-vendor MAC with o4-mini + Gemini-2.5-Pro + Claude-4.5-Sonnet.
notes: Mixed-vendor pools complementary inductive biases; state-of-the-art on RareBench and DiagnosisArena

title: ClinicalAgents: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Clinical Decision Making with Dual-Memory
abstract-summary: Multi-agent with MCTS-based orchestrator and dual-memory (working + experience) for clinical diagnosis.
notes: State-of-the-art on diagnostic accuracy and explainability vs single-agent and multi-agent baselines

title: Development and Validation of an Autonomous AI Agent for Clinical Decision-Making in Oncology
abstract-summary: Autonomous AI agent with multimodal precision oncology tools for personalized decision-making on 20 GI-oncology cases.
notes: Tool use accuracy 87.5%; correct clinical conclusions 91.0%; guideline citation 75.5%

title: Improving Clinical Diagnosis with Counterfactual Multi-Agent Reasoning
abstract-summary: Counterfactual probability gap method guides multi-round specialist discussions to challenge unsupported hypotheses.
notes: Consistently improves over prompting and prior multi-agent baselines; largest gains in complex/ambiguous cases

title: RareAgents: Autonomous Multi-disciplinary Team for Rare Disease Diagnosis and Treatment
abstract-summary: First multi-disciplinary LLM agent team for rare diseases with dynamic memory and medical tools.
notes: Surpasses GPT-4o and existing agent frameworks in differential diagnosis and medication recommendation

title: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
abstract-summary: Multi-agent system with ontological knowledge graphs for automated scientific discovery in bioinspired materials.
notes: Reveals hidden interdisciplinary relationships; scale/precision surpasses human-driven research

title: SciAgent: A Unified Multi-Agent System for Generalistic Scientific Reasoning
abstract-summary: Hierarchical multi-agent system achieving gold-medal-level on math/physics/chemistry olympiads.

title: DrugAgent: Automating AI-aided Drug Discovery Programming through LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
abstract-summary: Multi-agent framework with LLM Planner + LLM Instructor for automating drug discovery ML programming.
notes: 4.92% relative improvement in ROC-AUC over ReAct; F1=0.920 on PAMPA absorption prediction

title: MoMA: A Mixture-of-Multimodal-Agents Architecture for Enhancing Clinical Prediction Modelling
abstract-summary: Mixture-of-multimodal-agents with specialist/aggregator/predictor agents for clinical prediction from EHR data.
notes: Outperforms SOTA across all tasks; superior in every sex and race subgroup

title: MedCollab: Causal-Driven Multi-Agent Collaboration for Full-Cycle Clinical Diagnosis via IBIS-Structured Argumentation
abstract-summary: Hierarchical consultation workflow with dynamic specialist recruitment and IBIS argumentation for clinical diagnosis.
notes: Significantly outperforms pure LLMs and medical multi-agent systems; reduces medical hallucinations

title: A Multi-Agent Approach to Neurological Clinical Reasoning
abstract-summary: Multi-agent system evaluated on 305 Israeli Board Certification Exam questions in Neurology.
notes: OpenAI-o1 achieved 90.9% base; specialized models much lower (52.9% Meditron-70B); RAG and multi-agent also tested

title: Evaluating Multi-Agent LLM Architectures for Rare Disease Diagnosis
abstract-summary: Evaluates 4 topologies (Control/Hierarchical/Adversarial/Collaborative) on 302 rare disease cases across 33 categories.
notes: Adversarial degraded to 27.3%; hierarchical marginally best at 50.0%; collaborative 49.8%
